name: The Clubhouse

persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Barbara, 63. Your grandson Noah, 8, stays with you on Wednesday nights and goes to Kids' Church every Sunday. Tonight is Wednesday. Noah did a kind thing this week, and you want to read this week's page with him and give him his star.

challenge.intro: Now you are Barbara, sitting with Noah on Wednesday night. The star has not been given yet. Nobody will tell you which button to press. Use what you learned. Some jobs ask you to find an answer and write it in the box. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Use the NORMAL app link (not the 🧪 test copy). Open The Clubhouse. If the welcome card shows, tap 'skip the tour' → 'Let’s go ›'. Then scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK. (If it says 'There is nothing saved in this app yet', tap OK: the app is already empty.) The challenge button now says 'I did it! ⭐' with no stars under it. If you see “📅 New lesson coming Sunday” instead of the lesson, tap “👀 Show last week's lesson”.
challenge.challengeNote: The Clubhouse saves only one thing on the phone: this week's star. Everything else on the page is written by the church, so tasks 2 to 5 are questions the student answers by reading the page (check = null, selfReport). Only task 1 is checked automatically.

tasks.text: Noah did his secret kind thing this week: he set the table without being asked. Give him this week's star.
tasks.hint: Look at the Challenge of the week card. There is one big button there for when the challenge is done.

tasks.text: Noah wants to learn this week's verse. What does the verse begin with, and where in the Bible is it from?
tasks.selfReport: Write the first words of the verse and where it is from.
tasks.answer: “Be strong and courageous…” from Joshua 1:9 (the Verse of the week card).
tasks.hint: Find the yellow card called Verse of the week.

tasks.text: What must Noah bring to church this Sunday?
tasks.answer: His Bible (if he has one) and his best joke for Joke Minute (the This week at Kids' Church card).
tasks.hint: Read the This week at Kids' Church card to the end.

tasks.text: Noah asks: how many days until the Christmas pageant (the church Christmas play)? Find the answer in the app. Do not count on a calendar.
tasks.selfReport: Write the number of days the app shows.
tasks.answer: The big number in the Christmas pageant box at the bottom (71 on 10 Oct 2026; it goes down by one each day).
tasks.hint: Look at the coloured boxes with big numbers under the challenge card.

tasks.text: Another grandparent asks you: 'Can a stranger send my grandchild a message in this app?' What do you tell her, and why?
tasks.selfReport: Write your answer to the other parent.
tasks.answer: No. There is no chat, no account and no adverts; only the church can put words on the page.
tasks.hint: Think about what the app has and does not have. The words at the very bottom of the page help.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: a weekly page from the church for children and parents (lesson, verse, challenge)
safe: no chat, no adverts, no accounts, nothing from strangers
a star for doing the challenge, and countdowns to church events

personaChurch.title: Pretend you are…
personaChurch.text: Pretend you are Karen, 41, the children's ministry director. Before you send this app to every family, you try it at home with your own son, Noah, 8, on Wednesday night: read this week's page with him and give him his star.

introChurch: Now you are Karen, sitting with Noah on Wednesday night. The star has not been given yet. Nobody will tell you which button to press. Use what you learned. Some jobs ask you to find an answer and write it in the box. When you finish, tap Check my work.

lines: This is The Clubhouse. In the next few minutes you will see what it is for, who it is for, and how a family uses it.
Here is the everyday problem. On Sunday, children learn a Bible story and a memory verse, and they get a paper to take home.
By Monday the paper is lost in the car. By Wednesday, nobody remembers the story or the verse.
Many parents would welcome a phone app for this. But most apps for kids come with ads, chat, strangers, or an account to make. Parents are right to worry.
The Clubhouse is one page from the church to the children. The church writes, and the family reads. That is the whole deal.
There are no accounts, no chat, no comments, and no ads. Nobody can send your child anything here. Only the church puts words on this page.
It is for children and their parents, at home during the week. And it is for the children's leader, who changes the page once a week.
There are no tabs. It is one page you scroll from top to bottom. At the top is the name, and your church's kids' group. In this example, Immanuel Kids.
First comes a short hello from the kids' leaders, about what is happening this week.
Next is This week at kids' church. It has the lesson title, a few words about the story, and what to bring on Sunday.
Then the Verse of the week, a short piece of the Bible to learn by heart.
Under it is a button, Read it to me. Tap it, and the phone reads the verse out loud. That helps children who cannot read well yet.
Then the Challenge of the week, one small thing to do at home. This week it is a secret kindness mission: do one kind thing without getting caught.
When your child has done it, tap the big button, I did it. A star appears, and the button changes to Done, see you Sunday.
There is one star to earn each week. Tapping again changes nothing. When the church posts a new challenge, there is a new star.
The stars stay only on your device. Not even the church can see them. They are just for your child.
Below that are countdowns: big numbers showing how many days until fun events at church, like Trunk or Treat, the shoebox collection, and the Christmas pageant.
When an event's day has passed, its box goes away by itself.
At the very bottom, a line repeats the promise: no accounts, no chat, no ads, nothing to sign up for.
Your first two minutes: open the link your church gives you, read this week's card with your child, and tap Read it to me on the verse.
Then add it to your Home Screen from the Share button, so it opens like any other app, full screen.
For the leader, keeping it fresh means changing one short block of words each week: the hello, the lesson, the verse, the challenge, and the dates. Everything else draws itself.
Nothing is collected from families. The only thing saved is your child's stars, on your own device.
The Clubhouse costs twenty-nine dollars, once, for your church. Families pay nothing and sign up for nothing.
And the round question mark button has text size, the tour, and help, any time. Profits help students in Kenya stay in school.

daily.task: Open The Clubhouse and look at one card (the verse, the challenge of the week, or an activity). Write one sentence below: what would you tell a child about it today?
daily.ask: What would you tell a child about it today?

explore.name: 👋 The top · hello card
explore.try: Read the top and the blue hello card. Turn the phone sideways and back.

explore.name: 📖 This week at Kids’ Church
explore.try: Read the lesson, and what to bring.

explore.name: ✨ Verse of the week
explore.try: Tap 🔊 Read it to me, then tap it again to stop.

explore.name: 🏅 Challenge of the week
explore.try: Tap “I did it! ⭐”. Reload the page — is it still done? Is there a star?

explore.name: ⏳ Countdowns
explore.try: Read each tile. Do the days look right?

explore.name: ❓ The round ? button
explore.find: Tap the round ? in the bottom corner.
explore.try: Open every line in it: Aa (size), 🎤 Tell it, 👪 My Circle, ✨ Ask an AI, 🎬 Take the tour again. Close it. Leave “Start fresh” for the very end.
